label: Ptolemy's four seasonal lunar-syzygy markers
summary: In Tetrabiblos II.10, Ptolemy proposes using new- and full-moon syzygies preceding the four equinoctial and solstitial starting points to conjecture seasonal conditions for spring, summer, autumn and winter.

sources.title: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, Book II, Sections 10–13: Seasonal and Detailed Weather Predictions

label: Ptolemy's daily fixed-star weather intensifications
summary: In Tetrabiblos II.12, Ptolemy attributes day-by-day intensification of weather qualities chiefly to appearances of bright fixed stars at their morning or evening rising or setting relative to the Sun.

sources.title: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, Book II, Sections 10–13: Seasonal and Detailed Weather Predictions

label: Ptolemy's lunar halo weather signs
summary: In Tetrabiblos II.13, Ptolemy treats a single clear fading lunar halo as a fair-weather sign and multiple or differently colored and shaped lunar halos as signs of storms or winds.

sources.title: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, Book II, Sections 10–13: Seasonal and Detailed Weather Predictions

label: Aratus's early-crescent weather signs
summary: In Phaenomena, Aratus presents the shape and color of the Moon's horns on the third and fourth nights as signs for calm, wind, rain and storms, including directional winds linked to horn orientation.

sources.title: Aratus, Phaenomena: Zodiac Risings and Weather Signs

label: Aratus's Manger and Asses wind-rain signs
summary: Aratus states that a darkening or vanishing Manger in Cancer signals rain or storms, and that relative dimming of the northern or southern Ass star can indicate a southerly or northerly wind.

sources.title: Aratus, Phaenomena: Zodiac Risings and Weather Signs

label: Aratus's seabird and shorebird wind signs
summary: Aratus describes a heron flying landward from the sea with cries, storm petrels turning toward winds, and ducks or gulls beating wings on shore as signs preceding gales.

sources.title: Aratus, Phaenomena: Zodiac Risings and Weather Signs

label: Theophrastus's local mountain-cloud weather guidance
summary: Theophrastus says mountainous and coastal terrain affects cloud movements when winds change and advises attending to local conditions and knowledgeable local observers when interpreting weather signs.

label: Theophrastus's red-sky rain time window
summary: Theophrastus describes a reddish sky before sunrise as a rain sign for the same day or within three days, and a red sunset sky as a similar but less certain sign.

label: Theophrastus's ant-egg movement omens
summary: Theophrastus treats ants moving their eggs from hollow anthills to higher ground as a sign of rain and moving them down as a sign of fair weather.
